t:
Homework has long been a cornerstone of formal education. It reinforces concepts introduced in class, builds time-management skills, and gives teachers a window into students' understanding. Yet excessive homework can erode family time and sleep. Schools should therefore design assignments that are purposeful and limited in duration rather than merely abundant.

What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Homework is useful, but it must be purposeful and limited.
Homework should be abolished because it harms families.
Teachers should assign more homework to raise achievement.
Sleep is more important than any academic activity.

t:
In the past decade, remote work has shifted from a rare privilege to a routine arrangement. Employees report fewer commutes and greater control over their schedules. Managers, however, warn that informal mentoring and spontaneous collaboration are harder to sustain. Companies that blend remote and on-site work appear to capture the benefits of both models.

What can be inferred about a fully remote arrangement?
o: It offers no advantage to employees.
It is now the most common arrangement.

t:
Plastic straws are used for an average of twenty minutes yet persist in the environment for centuries. Coastal clean-ups repeatedly list them among the most common items collected. Consumers should refuse single-use straws and carry reusable alternatives. Small habits, multiplied by millions of people, produce measurable change.

What is the author's main purpose?
o: To describe how plastic straws are manufactured
To report the results of a scientific experiment
To persuade readers to stop using single-use straws
To compare plastic straws with paper cups

t:
Some educators argue that smartphones distract students and should be banned during lessons. Others counter that the devices provide instant access to dictionaries, simulations and collaborative platforms. A blanket ban, critics note, may punish responsible users while failing to teach digital discipline. The debate ultimately concerns not the device but the classroom culture that surrounds it.

What does the writer suggest about the smartphone debate?
o: A total ban is the only workable solution.
Teachers disagree about everything except discipline.
Smartphones have no legitimate academic use.
The real issue is classroom culture, not the device.

t:
The water cycle begins when the sun heats surface water, causing it to evaporate. This vapour rises, cools and condenses into droplets that form clouds. When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as precipitation, returning to rivers, lakes and soil. The cycle then repeats indefinitely.

In the sentence 'When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as precipitation', the word 'they' refers to ...

JAKARTA — A 6.2-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Sulawesi on Tuesday morning, prompting residents in three districts to evacuate to higher ground. No casualties have been reported, though several schools sustained minor damage. Authorities lifted the tsunami warning two hours later after sea levels returned to normal.

What is the passage mainly about?
o: The geological causes of earthquakes in Sulawesi
An earthquake that led to evacuation and a brief tsunami warning
The reconstruction of damaged schools in three districts
A tsunami that killed hundreds of residents

At first glance, the film's slow pacing feels like a flaw. By the final act, however, those quiet early scenes pay off, turning ordinary conversations into emotional landmines. The cinematography is restrained, the score almost invisible, and the lead performance carries the entire weight of the story. It is not a film for everyone, but it rewards patience.

When the old lighthouse keeper retired, the village expected the light to be automated within weeks. Instead, a teenager named Rani began climbing the tower every evening, oiling the mechanism and polishing the lens. She had no official appointment and received no wages. The ships, of course, never noticed the difference.

What can be inferred about Rani?
o: She was hired by the village government.
She was trained by the retired keeper.
She maintained the lighthouse out of personal commitment.

t:
The market opens before dawn, when the alleys are still damp and the air smells of wet asphalt and fried shallots. Vendors arrange pyramids of mangoes and stack baskets of chilli in colours so saturated they seem artificial. By nine, the crowd is impenetrable; by noon, only crushed leaves and cardboard remain.

The word 'impenetrable' in the passage is closest in meaning to ...
o: impossible to enter or pass through

t:
Extracting Clear Water in the Field
1. Dig a hole about 30 cm wide and 20 cm deep.
2. Place a container at the centre of the hole.
3. Cover the hole with a plastic sheet and seal the edges with soil.
4. Put a small stone on the centre of the sheet, directly above the container.
5. Leave the device under the sun for several hours.

Why is the stone placed on the centre of the sheet?
o: To keep the plastic sheet from blowing away
To press the sheet down so condensed water drips into the container
To measure the depth of the hole
To prevent insects from entering the container

Join 200,000 students who improved their scores last year.

What can be inferred about SmartLearn?
o: It is free of charge for all users.
It can only be used with a fast internet connection.

t:
The bar chart shows average daily study hours among Grade 12 students in four provinces: Province A 3.4 hours, Province B 2.1 hours, Province C 2.9 hours and Province D 1.6 hours. The national average is 2.5 hours.

Which statement is supported by the data?
o: Province B studied less than the national average.
All four provinces exceeded the national average.
Province C recorded the highest figure.
Province D recorded the lowest figure, below two hours.

t:
Dear Ms Harahap,
I am writing to apply for the position of Junior Data Analyst advertised on your company website on 3 May. I hold a degree in Statistics and have completed an internship in which I built dashboards for a retail client. I have attached my curriculum vitae and portfolio for your consideration.

What is the main purpose of the letter?
o: To apply for an advertised position
To recommend a colleague for promotion
To complain about a recruitment process
To offer a training programme to the company

t:
The greenhouse effect is often misunderstood. Certain gases in the atmosphere — carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour — allow shortwave solar radiation to pass through but absorb the longwave radiation the Earth emits. This absorbed energy warms the lower atmosphere. Without any greenhouse gases, the planet's average temperature would be roughly 33°C colder than it is today. The current concern is not the effect itself but its rapid intensification.

Which TWO statements are true according to the passage?
o: Greenhouse gases absorb longwave radiation emitted by the Earth.
The greenhouse effect is entirely harmful to the planet.
Without greenhouse gases, the Earth would be much colder.
Shortwave solar radiation is absorbed before it reaches the surface.

t:
SEMARANG — Heavy rain on Thursday night caused the Kaligarang river to overflow, inundating three sub-districts and forcing 400 residents into temporary shelters. The city's drainage system, built in the 1990s, was unable to handle the volume of water. Officials said repairs would begin next month, but residents argued that the problem has recurred every rainy season for a decade.

Which TWO statements are supported by the passage?
o: The drainage system was modernised last year.
The flooding is a recurring problem.
No residents were moved to shelters.

t:
Should schools require students to wear uniforms? Supporters contend that uniforms reduce visible inequality and simplify daily decisions. Opponents argue that they suppress self-expression and that the cost of official sets can burden low-income families. Research offers no decisive verdict: some studies link uniforms to improved attendance, others find no academic effect. Most schools, in practice, compromise — requiring a uniform on certain days while permitting casual dress on others.

Which THREE statements are stated in the passage?
o: Supporters say uniforms reduce visible inequality.
Opponents mention the financial burden on poor families.
Research consistently proves that uniforms raise grades.
Many schools adopt a compromise policy.

t:
Every morning Pak Sudirman opened his shop at five, though no customer had ever arrived before seven. He swept the floor, arranged the tins in perfect rows, and waited. When his daughter asked why he bothered, he said only that a shop should look as if it expects good things. Years later, after the road was widened and most stalls closed, customers still came to his.

Which TWO statements are supported by the passage?
o: He opened the shop earlier than any customer arrived.
He closed the shop because the road was widened.
He believed a shop should look as though it expects success.
His daughter eventually took over the business.

t:
Solar panels are frequently criticised for producing nothing at night. Yet this objection ignores how electricity grids actually work. Panels generate most during the day, when demand from offices and factories peaks, and storage or gas plants cover the evening. The real barrier to wider adoption is not intermittency but the upfront cost of installation, which many households cannot finance without long-term loans.

Which TWO statements are supported by the passage?
o: The writer regards intermittency as the main barrier to adoption.
Solar output peaks at the same time as daytime demand.
The cost of installation limits wider adoption.
Gas plants become unnecessary in grids that use solar panels.
